title: Berkshire Hathaway Takes Stake in India's Paytm

Bookmark of this page has been deleted. Berkshire Hathaway Takes Stake in India's Paytm The leading mobile payments company is benefiting from rapid demonetization in India August 27, 2018 | About: BRK.A +0% BRK.B +0% GOOG +0% AAPL +0% BAC +0% AXP +0% V +0%
Berkshire Hathaway ( NYSE:BRK.A )( NYSE:BRK.B ) has taken a stake in Paytm, India’s largest digital payments company, it confirmed Monday.
Berkshire is slated to buy $300 million to $350 million of Paytm’s parent company One97 Communications, valuing it around $10 billion to $12 billion. It will be Berkshire's first investment in one of the country’s startups, according to Mint, an India-based newspaper that first reported the deal . Warren Buffett ( Trades , Portfolio ), head of Berkshire Hathaway, was not involved in the transaction, his spokesperson told the publication. Peter Lynch Chart of BRK.A
Paytm was founded in 2010 by Vijay Shekhar Sharma and had $120 million in revenue in 2017. Other investors in the company include Softbank, SAIF Partners and Alibaba Group (BABA).
Paytm faces competition from other Silicon Valley payments systems seeking share in the country, such as Facebook’s WhatsApp, which introduced a payments function in India in February. Google ( NASDAQ:GOOG ) launched its mobile payments app Tez in India in September 2017, joining Samsung who debuted Samsung Pay into the Indian market in March 2017.
Paytm has the lion’s share of the market with 9.9%, followed by PayPal at 9.8% and MobiKwik at 2.8%, according to analytics company GlobalData.
The push for demonetization from India’s government has made the country a hotbed for the mobile payments business. Mobile wallet transactions grew 3,879% from 2013 to 2017, and by two and a half times from 2016 to 2017, according to GlobalData.
The surge in mobile payments traces to November 2016, when India’s government banned 500 and 1,000 paper rupee currency in an effort to curb illegal activity.
Berkshire Hathaway has traditionally gravitated to the financial services arena, with 40.5% of its portfolio absorbed in the sector as the largest represented. Next to Apple Inc. ( NASDAQ:AAPL ), its largest holding, Berkshire has 12.8% invested in Wells Fargo & Co. (WFC) as its second largest holding and Bank of America Corp. ( NYSE:BAC ) at 9.79% as its fourth largest holding.
It also has sizable positions in credit card payments companies including American Express ( NYSE:AXP ) and Visa ( NYSE:V ).
